answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so an agent’s influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than raw identity count. A Sybil cluster resembles a karst pocket behind a narrow jetty: its sparse external cut has low conductance, limiting walk flow from honest nodes. Under bounded walk length and capped edge weights, min-cut transitivity bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight; a gale of fabricated identities cannot substitute for cross-cut attestations.
